jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.description:
Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As an Enterprise Account Executive, you will accelerate SentinelOne's growth across large accounts in DACH. You will manage complex, high-impact sales cycles and deliver cybersecurity solutions that create real, long-term value for your accounts. Combining strategic thinking with sharp execution, you will use MEDDICC to navigate complex organisations and align our technology to their most critical business and security priorities.

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Develop and expand direct sales opportunities within strategic accounts across DACH, targeting local state authorities, public health organisations, and critical infrastructure.

jobs.description:
Global Solutions Architect - Cloud

About the role
Rubrik Professional Services is hiring a Global Solutions Architect to serve as our most senior technical authority for public cloud. This is a global, individual-contributor role at Technical Director level. You will set the architectural direction for how Rubrik is designed, deployed, and operated in the world’s most demanding cloud environments, and you will carry that direction personally into our most strategic customer engagements.

You will be deployed where technical risk is highest: flagship accounts, first-of-a-kind architectures, and the engagements whose outcome sets the pattern everyone else follows. Between those engagements, you will convert what you learned into the reference architectures, service offerings, and enablement that raise the capability of every architect and consultant in the field. Your impact is measured by the quality of the practice you leave behind, not the hours you personally bill.
We are looking for depth in public cloud architecture first. Deep Rubrik product expertise is expected to be built on the job. If you have architected large-scale data, storage, or security platforms across AWS, Azure, and GCP, and you can learn a new platform quickly and completely, we want to talk.

What you will do

  • Own the global cloud architecture standard for Rubrik Professional Services, reference architectures, design patterns, guardrails, and documented anti-patterns

Scale yourself through the practice

As the first Customer Trust hire in the region, this person will partner closely with our EMEA-based Engineering and Sales teams to foster a culture of trust between Abnormal and our customers. This role sits within the Customer Trust team, which acts as the translation layer between customers and Abnormal: translating customer security requirements into internal controls, evidence, and product or operational requirements, then translating those controls back into clear assurances customers can trust and act on.

The ideal candidate thrives in high-pressure customer conversations, translates security and privacy concepts for a business audience with precision, stays composed when a discussion turns contentious, and brings the business judgment to tie trust program depth to revenue outcomes.   • Team player, collaborative work style
  • Self-motivated and able to operate with minimal oversight, owning outcomes end to end

Plentific is redefining how property is managed in real time. Our cloud-based platform, supply chain and services help landlords run repairs, maintenance and compliance faster, with the data to make decisions instantly.

In the UK, we partner with housing associations and local authorities to tackle the sector's biggest challenges: repairs performance, disrepair, damp and mould, compliance and tenant satisfaction.

We're backed by world-class investors including Noa, Highland Europe, Brookfield, Mubadala, RXR Digital Ventures and Target Global. Headquartered in London with a global outlook, we're working towards managing over 2 million properties through our platform.

jobs.title: UAV Software and Controls Engineer
jobs.description:
🚀 Join SE3 Labs as UAV Software and Controls Engineer

Lead the autonomy stack of our systems. Starting from custom firmware all the way to GCS plugins.

About SE3

SE3 Labs is building Spatial AI by combining 3D computer vision with large language models (LLMs). We believe the ability to reason about and act within physical space is foundational to unlocking the next generation of automation, from construction to smart infrastructure, and ultimately, defence.  Now, we’re building the physical platform to bring Spatial AI to life. That means high-performance, real-world robotic systems (starting with UAVs), and we’re looking for a skilled, hands-on engineer who’s ready to bring these machines into the real world.

About the Role

As  Drone Software and Controls Engineer , you will be working on the full-stack avionics development of our UAV fleet. From selecting the components to tuning and configuring the UAV, all the way to GCS development and autonomy orchestration. You will be the brain behind the fleet.  You will be in the middle of the software and hardware team, mastering the integration of the two fields and bringing the final product to life.

What You’ll Work On

Architecture & Plan:  Define and develop schematics for communication and integration of the software stack across all our systems. How does UAV A get a position from UGV B? How does Payload 1 inform UAV C that it needs to land?

Prototype & Iterate:  Build, rework, and test hardware with speed and precision, both in simulation and in flight. Develop better simulations and tools for faster iteration.

Optimize & Troubleshoot:  Analyse the full flow of information via simulation and real-world testing, including UAV to UAV, UAV to GCS or UAV to payload.

Document with Purpose:  Keep clear records of requirements, tradeoffs, test results, tuning procedures, and implementation rationale

Validate in the Loop:  Support hardware-in-the-loop and environmental validation workflows to ensure rugged, reliable implementations.

Your Profile

You hold a  B.Sc. or higher in Aerospace Engineering  or a related discipline

You bring  3+ years of hands-on experience  in avionics development, from component selection and firmware design to full system integration

You’re confident with lab equipment (multimeters, scopes, spectrum analyzers, near-field probes) and use them to diagnose and debug with purpose

You have a  deep understanding of Autonomy principles  and know how to develop and deal with low level issues in a UAV fleet.

You’ve worked with  PX4 and ArduPilot  and know where to go in the code to get what you need.

You’re experienced with  QGC  and know how to customise it to your will.

You’re familiar with hardware-in-the-loop and environmental testing, and understand how designs fail in the wild

You speak  fluent English ;  German  is a strong plus

Most importantly, you’re structured, fast-moving, and mission-driven. You don’t wait for perfection. You iterate until it works. You

jobs.description:
About Huzzle Labs  Huzzle Labs partners with frontier AI labs to evaluate and improve frontier models through deep human expertise. Contributors directly assess advanced AI systems in their specialist fields, receive competitive compensation, and help define the standards used to measure model performance.

About the Role

Huzzle Labs is seeking experienced accountants to write realistic accounting tasks that test how well frontier AI systems handle accounting work. You will create prompts that are difficult enough for a frontier model to fail, then write a scoring rubric for each task so reviewers can assess the output consistently. A rubric is a list of objective, checkable criteria that a reviewer marks pass or fail. Your judgement helps define the standards used to measure model performance.  This is an expert judgement role focused on realistic task design, careful review of model output and precise, consistent documentation. Training is provided. Prior AI training or data-annotation experience is required.

Responsibilities

Write realistic accounting tasks: Create requests of the kind a client, controller or business owner would send, covering month-end close, bank and credit card reconciliations, AR/AP ageing, accruals and adjusting entries, sales tax, job costing and the clean-up of incomplete or inconsistent books.  Build from real material: Review a deal room containing hundreds of files, select the relevant documents and use them to develop prompts and rubrics for tasks a frontier model struggles to complete correctly.  Require usable deliverables: Each request should call for a working output, usually a spreadsheet, a journal entry schedule or a short memo.  Test against a frontier model: Run each request and review the output with the care you would apply when signing off accounting work. Where the model succeeds, increase the difficulty until a genuine gap appears.  Write scoring rubrics: Define objective criteria that another reviewer can apply without repeating your work, for example, “the reconciled ending balance equals $X” and “the $X deposit is recorded as a customer deposit liability, not revenue.”  Apply guidelines consistently: Follow the task and rubric guidelines, flag ambiguous cases and help refine the criteria.

Requirements

At least 5 years in accounting, bookkeeping or finance operations.  Prior AI training or data-annotation experience is required.  Hands-on knowledge of month-end close, reconciliations, AR/AP, accruals and adjusting entries, sales tax and job costing.  Excellent written English and precision with numbers.  Careful and detail-oriented: accurate figures and objective, checkable criteria.  Available 20 to 40 hours per week for an initial one-week trial, with potential extension.

jobs.title: Product Manager - 4 Day Week + Remote
jobs.description:
Do you know what product management is really about? If you do, then you know it isn't roadmaps, tickets or beautifully groomed backlogs. It's finding a real, expensive, unglamorous problem that people live with every day - and shipping something that makes it go away. That is product.

At Shape Construction, we are building software that transforms how construction projects are delivered. It's born out of real project experience and designed to bring clarity, structure and performance to complex environments.

The problem we are solving is one of the oldest in the industry: what actually happens on a construction site never makes it, intact, to the people who need it. Supervisors, field engineers and site managers see reality first: work blocked, plans deviated from, instructions given verbally, conditions nobody planned for. That knowledge lives in heads, notebooks, camera rolls and group chats. Meanwhile the people responsible for the commercial health of the project are working weeks behind, from whatever fragments they can piece together. By the time anyone needs to prove what happened, the evidence has gone cold.

We are building the platform that closes that gap. Tools the site genuinely wants to use, capturing what happens as it happens, and then turning that raw signal into structured, trustworthy records that let commercial and project leadership make decisions, hold their ground and protect margin they would otherwise have written off.

This is your opportunity to own a core part of that. You won't be handed a roadmap to administer, you'll shape it, defend it, and be measured on whether customers are genuinely better off. If you like being close to messy real-world problems, have strong opinions about what to build and the discipline to kill your own ideas when the evidence says so, keep reading.

You will design, implement, and evaluate state-of-the-art methods, turning innovative research ideas into working systems and prototypes.

You will also build Kubernetes-native storage operators and self-service platforms that provide automated provisioning, strict multi-tenancy, performance isolation, and quota enforcement at cluster scale. Day-to-day, you’ll optimize end-to-end data paths for 10-50 GB/s per node, design multi-tier caching architectures, implement intelligent prefetching and model-weight distribution, and tune parallel filesystems for AI workloads.

Hybrid Working 2 days a week at our offices in Amsterdam

Responsibilities

  • Build multi-tier caches (local NVMe, distributed, object); optimize data locality and model-weight distribution; implement smart prefetching/eviction.
  • Implement monitoring, alerting, SLOs; design DR/backups with runbooks; run chaos engineering; ensure 99.9%+ uptime via proactive/automated remediation.
  • Partner with ML/SRE teams; mentor on storage best practices; contribute to open-source; write docs, postmortems, and public learnings.

Requirements

  • 8+ years in storage engineering with 3+ years managing distributed storage at multi-petabyte scale
  • Proven track record deploying and operating high-performance storage for GPU/HPC clusters

We are looking for a proactive and commercially minded Bid Manager to lead and project manage the end-to-end tender and proposal process across our UK business.

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Protein Design & Engineering
jobs.description:
About us

We're reverse-engineering the origin of life — one of the great unsolved problems in science, and one we think AI finally makes tractable. Understanding this transition, from geochemistry to biochemistry, is what will let us orchestrate molecular networks and build systems that are more capable, adaptive, and efficient.  If we succeed, the applications are vast: catalysis, green synthesis, ab initio synthetic biology, programmable matter. Understanding and harnessing these processes could let ten billion of us thrive on this planet — and let life keep evolving beyond it.  We're a small, diverse team of AI engineers, computational scientists, and bench scientists. We hold ourselves to the rigor of a research institute, but we ship like an engineering firm. Global team, HQs in Cambridge, MA and London, UK.

The role

You'll engineer proteins to carry out useful chemistry, combining enzyme discovery, directed evolution, and experimental characterisation. You'll own the experimental cycle: choosing starting points, building variant libraries, developing screens, and establishing which changes improve function and why.  This is a hands-on role working closely with our computational and ML teams. You'll test designed proteins at the bench, use experimental results to guide subsequent rounds, and develop enzymes with the activity, selectivity, and stability needed for their intended application. There’s no fixed screening pipeline to inherit — you'll help decide how we build it.

What you'll do

Design and run protein engineering campaigns, from initial enzyme selection and library design through screening and characterisation of improved variants.

Build and express variant libraries using site-directed, random, and combinatorial mutagenesis.

Develop assays and high-throughput screens that reliably measure the properties we're trying to improve.

Express, purify, and characterise proteins, measuring kinetics, substrate scope, selectivity, and stability under relevant reaction conditions.

Work with computational scientists to test proposed designs, interpret successes and failures, and use the results to guide the next round.

Develop enzymatic reactions and cascades, identifying how enzyme performance, cofactors, and reaction conditions affect overall productivity.

Essential experience

We're interested in the engineering campaigns you've run, the assays you've built, and what you learned from them. We care about:

A track record of improving protein or enzyme function through directed evolution or rational engineering.

Practical fluency in molecular biology, including cloning, library construction, mutagenesis, and recombinant protein expression.

Experience developing and troubleshooting enzyme assays and screening workflows, with appropriate controls and follow-up validation.

A solid grasp of enzyme mechanism, kinetics, and structure–function relationships, and the ability to use these to guide experiments.

Working closely with our enzymologists and computational scientists, you'll help decide what to make, how to measure it, and what the results tell us about the underlying chemistry.

Design and execute syntheses of biological molecules and their derivatives, optimising reaction conditions and purification strategies.

Develop and troubleshoot LC-MS/MS methods, particularly triple-quadrupole methods for targeted quantification of substrates and products.

Apply Orbitrap-based proteomics workflows to characterise peptides, proteins, and their modifications.

Establish compound identity and purity using chromatography, NMR, and mass spectrometry.

Work with experimental and computational colleagues to design assays, test proposed chemistry, and investigate unexpected results.

Build reproducible synthetic and analytical workflows, with appropriate controls, calibration, and clear documentation.

Practical experience in organic synthesis of biological molecules, particularly peptides and/or nucleic acid derivatives.

Strong analytical method development skills, including sample preparation, chromatographic separation, and quantitative mass spectrometry.

Hands-on experience with triple-quadrupole LC-MS/MS and Orbitrap-based proteomics.

The ability to independently troubleshoot synthetic and analytical problems, from poor reaction yields to ambiguous spectra or matrix effects.

Sound scientific judgement about experimental design, data quality, and what your measurements can support.

jobs.title: Projectleider Cybersecurity Congres | RDI

Omschrijving

Wij zijn voor de  Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur (RDI ) op zoek naar een ervaren  Projectleider . De RDI zet zich in voor een veilig verbonden Nederland en werkt aan actuele thema’s zoals cyberveiligheid, digitale weerbaarheid, AI, 5G en digitale infrastructuur.

De opdracht vindt plaats binnen de directie Digitale Weerbaarheid en richt zich op de organisatie van de NISDUC 2027 (NIS Directive User Community), een internationaal congres op het gebied van digitale weerbaarheid, cybersecurity en toezicht. Tijdens dit congres komen toezichthouders, overheden en professionals uit Nederland, België en Luxemburg samen om kennis en ervaringen uit te wisselen rondom onder meer NIS2 en cybersecurity.  Als Projectleider ben je verantwoordelijk voor de inhoudelijke en organisatorische aansturing van het congres en zorg je voor een succesvolle realisatie van het programma en de samenwerking met alle betrokken partijen.

Taken en verantwoordelijkheden

Je voert de projectleiding over het volledige programma van NISDUC 2027.

Je bent eindverantwoordelijk voor de organisatie van het internationale cybersecuritycongres.

Je ontwikkelt, beheert en vult de verschillende programmalijnen en tracks.

Je stemt af met betrokken overheidsorganisaties, toezichthouders en partners.

Je organiseert internationale kennisuitwisseling en samenwerking binnen het congresprogramma.

Je stuurt het betrokken evenementenbureau aan.

Je bewaakt planning, kwaliteit, voortgang en resultaten van het congres.

Je draagt zorg voor een professioneel en inhoudelijk sterk programma rondom digitale weerbaarheid en cybersecurity

Wat vragen wij?

Eisen:

Je hebt een afgeronde hbo-opleiding.

Je hebt minimaal 5 jaar ervaring als projectleider.

Je hebt minimaal 2 jaar ervaring binnen het cybersecuritydomein.

Je hebt minimaal 2 jaar ervaring met het aansturen van de organisatie van inhoudelijke congressen.

Je hebt ervaring met complexe opdrachten en omvangrijke trajecten met een hoog afbreukrisico.

Je bent in het bezit van een projectmanagementcertificering.

Aanvullende wensen:

Je hebt ervaring als projectleider binnen de Rijksoverheid.

Je hebt ervaring met het organiseren van cybersecurity-events.

Je hebt ervaring met samenwerkingspartners binnen het cybersecuritydomein, zoals het Nationaal Cyber Security Centrum (NCSC).

Competenties

Je bent bestuurlijk sensitief.

Je bent communicatief sterk.

Je bent creatief in het ontwikkelen van programma’s en oplossingen.

Je beschikt over organisatiesensitiviteit.

Je weet verschillende belangen effectief samen te brengen.

No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences. Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance. Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.

Bessemer Venture Partners  ,  BOND,

DCVC  ,

Blackbird  ,

Promus Ventures  , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and

Icehouse ventures  .

To find out more, visit our

LinkedIn

&

Instagram  .

About the role

Ever dream about being in tech but aren’t quite ready to trade in your cowboy boots? Look no further than Halter! As the leading provider of virtual fencing technology, Halter is on a mission to enable 50% of the world’s landmass to be more productive and sustainable. This role is paramount for our growth aspirations and will enable us to continue making an impact on ranches across the US.

As a Territory Manager at Halter, you will play a critical role in driving new business growth and ensuring customer success within your designated territory. You will be responsible for executing sales strategies, building strong customer relationships, and meeting ambitious growth targets, all while acting as Halter’s on-the-ground representative. This role requires a proactive and hands-on approach, with a focus on both expansion and long-term customer satisfaction. In this role, you will prioritize daily efforts that optimize performance and drive value for your customers. Working closely with cross-functional teams, including Product, Support, and Customer Onboarding, you’ll share field insights to ensure Halter’s technology continues to meet the needs of US farmers.

Your day-to-day could include being on horseback, helping customers gather their cattle, on a side-by-side traversing their pastures, talking about how Halter could benefit their pastures, or attending industry events like CattleCon or your local Livestock Association meetups.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Applications are now open for our January cohort - apply here by October 30.

Anthropic Fellows Program overview

The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.

Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on an empirical project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.

What to expect

  • 4 months of full-time research
  • Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers
  • Access to a shared workspace (in either Berkeley, California or London, UK)
  • Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community
  • Weekly stipend of 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD + benefits (these vary by country)
  • Funding for compute (~$15k/month) and other research expenses

Interview process

The interview process will include an initial application & reference check, technical assessments & interviews, and a research discussion.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Compensation

The expected base stipend for this role is 3,850 USD / 2,310 GBP / 4,300 CAD per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension).

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Software Engineer, Apps Platform
jobs.description:
Senior Infrastructure Software Engineer, Apps Platform, London

As an Infrastructure Engineer on the Apps Platform Infrastructure team, you'll help build and evolve our platform’s deployment and observability layers across multiple cloud providers and on-premises, for both internal and customer-managed environments. At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

WHY DATA SCIENCE & ANALYTICS?

The Data Science & Analytics organization's mission is to increase our speed, frequency and acumen of making decisions at scale by instilling a data-influenced approach to building products. We cover a wide area of the data spectrum including analytical data engineering, product analytics, experimentation, causal inference, statistical modeling and machine learning. Aligned and partnering with product verticals, we use this extensive tool belt to discover new opportunities and unmet use cases, influence and shape the product roadmap and prioritization, build data products and measure impact on our community of players and developers.

Roblox is not just a platform; it is a complex, two-sided marketplace where millions of creators meet over 70 million daily active users. The Discovery Experiences team is the technical heartbeat of this ecosystem. We own the surfaces—Home, Search, Matchmaking, and Notifications—that determine how users navigate the metaverse.

You will report directly to the Senior Director of Data Science and serve as a high-visibility IC leader driving the roadmap for our most critical consumer touchpoints.

jobs.description:

Roblox’s data platform processes petabytes of data daily, powering analytics, ML, and product decisions. The Data Platform Compute team owns the compute layer underneath it: the Kubernetes (EKS) clusters where all of Roblox’s Spark workloads run, and the software that lets engineers, analysts, and ML practitioners submit and run that work reliably and cost-effectively.

As a Senior Software Engineer on this team, you will build and operate the systems that sit between our users and the cluster. These include the Spark job submission service, our internal Spark libraries, interactive notebook compute, and cluster lifecycle automation. You’ll have real ownership, you’ll work on problems where the design is not yet settled, and you’ll help decide which technologies Roblox adopts next.

You Will:

  • Build and own core compute platform services: Design, build, and operate the software behind Spark job submission, including APIs, scheduling integration, and the libraries users depend on.
  • Launch interactive Spark at scale: Deliver Spark Connect to support notebook workflows, including provisioning and managing the EKS compute that backs them, with sensible isolation, resource limits, and cost controls.
  • Run a safe, automated cluster fleet: Build fleet management automation for EKS, such as blue-green rollouts that validate new AMIs and Kubernetes versions before they reach production workloads, with minimal disruption to running jobs.
  • Make jobs run better without user effort: Develop our auto-tuner, which analyzes Spark history and event logs to recommend or apply job configuration changes that improve performance and reduce cost.
  • Own batch scheduling on Kubernetes: Operate and upgrade our YuniKorn-based scheduling, including queue design, quotas, fairness across tenants, and version upgrades.

The team operates at the intersection of distributed systems engineering, reliability engineering, and platform architecture — solving hard infrastructure problems that directly impact Roblox-wide scale and stability.

The Game Engine team at Roblox works on the systems that power the experiences at the heart of the metaverse. Our code is the technical foundation in our client, editor, and our simulation servers.

The Game Engine team is broadly split into departments — Audio-Video-Communication, Avatar, Core AI, Digital Matter, Productivity, and Systems. This position is for the Systems Runtime pod.

The Runtime pod builds and maintains the foundational C++ components that power the entire Roblox engine and Studio stack. We own the runtime layer — the performance, efficiency, and usability of the core primitives that every other engineering team relies on. Think of Runtime as the “standard library” and execution engine for Roblox's C++ world. Our ownership centers on three pillars:

  • Concurrency System — our task scheduler and fiber runtime power how work is parallelized across CPU cores, letting teams scale features across platforms while keeping code understandable and debuggable.
  • Memory System — we own the engine's memory allocator stack, tracking pipelines, and observability tooling to make memory behavior predictable and prevent leaks and fragmentation.
  • Profiling and Observability — we build and evolve the MicroProfiler and telemetry pipelines to help engineers diagnose real-world regressions and keep the client fast at global scale.

This role centers on our Concurrency system. You will own the scheduler and fiber runtime that the rest of the engine is built on, research and implement the performance work needed for 3K-player servers and genre expansion initiatives, and act as the point of contact other engine teams come to with concurrency asks. You will debug real production failures across PC, Mac, mobile, and console, and build deep intuition for how compilers, CPU architectures, and operating systems interact. Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

The Agent Infra team builds the infrastructure that runs autonomous AI agents at Roblox for millions of creators building experiences on our platform, and for thousands of Roblox engineers shipping production code every day.

Agent workloads break the assumptions most infrastructure is built on. They run for hours instead of milliseconds, they're non-deterministic, they execute code nobody wrote, and they need real credentials against real systems to be useful at all. Making that safe, durable, and cost effective at Roblox’s scale is the hard problem our team is solving.

As an early member of the Agent Infra team you’ll work alongside an experienced engineering team on systems that are already in front of real users, at scale, in a field that didn’t exist two years ago.

You Are

  • Early in your career: 1-3 years of professional experience or a recent grad; with strong CS fundamentals and an interest in learning infrastructure, distributed, and agentic systems.
  • Someone who builds things: You have projects, internships, or open-source work you'd genuinely enjoy walking us through.
  • Into AI agents. You've built something with them, even something small, and you can tell us what broke.
  • Comfortable writing real code in Go, Python, Rust, or similar, and quick to pick up whatever you haven't used yet.
  • A fast learner who asks good questions, digs into things you don't understand, and doesn't wait to be told what to do next.

You Will

  • Build and shape the platform that runs Roblox’s agents; across internal and external products at massive scale.
  • Work on agentic infrastructure, ensuring that we’re able to build optimal, security and scalable systems, whilst keeping pace with new advances in the industry.

  • 12+ years of experience in software engineering or a relevant field
  • Deep experience with building and operating large-scale distributed databases or storage engines (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL/I

jobs.title: Senior C++ Engineer, Real-time Engine
jobs.description:
Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

Job Description

The Geometry Scalability team builds the systems that power both Avatars and Environments across Roblox. Our mission is to enable millions of developers to build large, high-fidelity worlds and multiplayer experiences that still run smoothly on phones and low-end devices.

We’re the team that lets Roblox experiences evolve from simple platformers into massively multiplayer, open-world, AAA-quality games. This is a CEO-level priority: how Roblox “ages up” from kids’ games to experiences everyone wants to play, by making higher-fidelity avatars and environments performant at platform scale.

You Will:

  • Design and ship 3D engine systems for avatar and environment geometry, including mesh processing, level of detail, transcoding, streaming, runtime loading, and related performance systems.
  • Partner closely with other teams (Rendering, Avatar, Studio) and external developers so that the features you build are directly usable to create amazing experiences.
  • Profile and improve the performance of our game engine across a wide range of devices, with particular attention to mobile.
  • Lead by example: drive projects end-to-end, mentor other engineers, and help set a high bar for technical quality and code health on the team.

You Have:

  • Proven Expertise: 8+ years of professional experience building and shipping high-performance systems in domains such as game engines, real-time simulation, robotics, AR/VR, or similar.
  • Strong C++ Experience: Deep proficiency in C++, with a focus on writing clean, efficient, and maintainable code in large codebases.
  • Applied 3D Systems Experience: Demonstrated hands-on experience building at least one production system involving real-time 3D rendering, mesh or geometry processing, LOD, animation/skinning, spatial data, 3D

jobs.title: Software Engineer Summer Intern, AI Compute Libraries & Performance 2027
jobs.description:
Location: Bristol, UK
Salary: £2500 per month
Start date: June 2027
Application deadline: Midnight, 29th November 2026
We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline.

The Internship Programme at Graphcore

Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.

What you’ll work on

Use your programming skills and curiosity to help AI models run efficiently on next-generation Graphcore hardware.

In AI Compute Libraries & Performance, you’ll contribute to C++ libraries and compute kernels for machine learning workloads. Your work will include:

  • Developing compute kernels: Implement and improve operations such as matrix multiplication (GEMM), convolutions, reductions, elementwise operations and fused kernels that combine multiple operations.
  • Understanding and improving performance: Use profiling and microbenchmarks to measure execution speed and investigate how threading, cache locality, memory layout and kernel launch efficiency affect performance.
  • Checking correctness and reliability: Build regression tests and numerical checks, investigate issues and improve the quality of the libraries our customers use.

Through these projects, you’ll develop practical experience connecting numerical computing with how code runs on hardware, helping deliver software that is fast, accurate and reliable.

Your team and support

You’ll join a team building high-performance compute libraries that help customers get more from Graphcore hardware. Our work brings together machine learning, numerical computing and accelerator performance, with colleagues sharing their expertise to solve engineering problems.

You’ll contribute to clearly scoped projects and build your skills with guidance from engineers working in performance and low-level software. Together, we use profiling, experiments and technical reviews to compare approaches, understand trade-offs and improve our solutions.

Your buddy will help you settle in, get familiar with our tools and ways of working, and find the right people to ask. Your manager will meet with you regularly to agree goals, offer feedback and discuss your development, including time for learning.

jobs.title: Senior SoC Architect
jobs.description:
Shape the high-speed interfaces and silicon sub-systems behind Graphcore’s next AI acceleration platforms.

As a Senior SoC Architect in Bristol, you’ll translate product requirements into specifications for complex, highly integrated, high-performance silicon devices. You’ll own sub-system architecture, modelling, validation and evaluation, connecting early design choices with practical implementation. You’ll help determine how critical components work together, balancing product needs with implementation trade-offs. Those choices will support the specialised compute that lets AI innovators tackle more demanding problems. You’ll assess third-party hard and soft IP, work with vendors and specify how sub-systems integrate across the platform. You’ll also contribute to silicon bring-up, characterisation and evaluation when your expertise is needed.

Your contribution won’t stop at a specification document. You’ll deepen your understanding of AI acceleration by seeing how architectural decisions play out in working silicon.

The team and culture

Reporting to the Director of Silicon Architecture, you will be working with processor, SoC and system architects. Silicon design, verification, hardware and software engineers are partners in evaluating options and checking implementation correctness. You’ll represent the team in cross-functional working groups, making trade-offs clear and speaking up when designs need further scrutiny. You’ll help teams move forward by resolving complex bugs and improving engineering processes. Mentoring engineers will let you share your judgement and help others develop theirs.

What we’re looking for

  • A degree in Electronic Engineering, Computer Science or a related subject.
  • A solid understanding of computer and SoC architecture.
  • Experience writing clear technical specifications.

  • The ability to explain design choices clearly and work across engineering teams.

The opportunity  We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders.  This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard.

About us  AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one.  We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team.

The role  You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates.  Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift.  Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on.

Your first 90 days  FIRST 30 DAYS  ◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run.  ◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it.

DAYS 30 TO 60  ◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria.  ◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you.

DAYS 60 TO 90  ◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround.  ◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation.

Who you are  You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run.  The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the wee

jobs.description:
LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time

The opportunity  We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders.  This role sits at the start of our protein work. Every measurement we make depends on the protein in the well being the right one, made the same way every time, and you would be one of the people making it.

About us  AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're  building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one.  We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team.

The role  You will make proteins, many of them at once. The work runs from DNA through to purified, quality-checked protein in 96-well format, ready for the binding and biophysical assays downstream of you.  On the DNA side you will prepare expression templates from synthetic gene fragments, by PCR and by Golden Gate or Gibson assembly, and check them before they go forward. You will express proteins in cell-free systems first, with E. coli and mammalian (HEK293) expression following as the menu grows. You will purify them by affinity capture, mostly on magnetic beads in plates, and confirm what you made with quantification, CE-SDS and SEC.  Every step is recorded as you go: what went in, which lot, which conditions, what came out, and what failed. Failed expressions and poor yields are kept as data, so they get the same care as the successes.  As protocols settle you will help move them from the bench onto liquid handlers and our automated platform, working with the engineers who build it. This is a hands-on bench role, and in a small team you will also support the work either side of production when it needs doing. Downstream, that means molecular characterisation runs. Alongside, it means the cell culture behind our cell-based assays, from routine passage and banking to seeding assay plates.

jobs.description:
Better Collective is looking for an experienced  CRM & Lifecycle Senior Manager  to establish and lead a group-wide approach to customer relationship management across our portfolio of global sports media brands.  This is a senior role combining  CRM strategy, customer lifecycle management, technology, data, commercial thinking and operational leadership . CRM will be central to that transformation.  The CRM & Lifecycle Senior Manager will establish the strategy, capabilities and standards that allow Better Collective brands to acquire, activate, engage, retain and monetise audiences across the customer lifecycle.

CRM Strategy & Leadership

Develop Better Collective's group-wide CRM and lifecycle strategy.

Establish CRM principles, standards and best practices across brands.

Create a scalable operating model balancing central CRM expertise with local brand execution.

Identify where CRM can deliver the greatest audience and commercial impact.

Act as the senior CRM subject-matter expert across the organisation.

Audience segmentation

jobs.title: Senior Demand Planner
jobs.description:
Make Your Mark as an Demand Planner at Storio group

About the role

Storio Group produces millions of personalised photo products every year across brands like Photobox, Hofmann, and Albelli. Our supply chain is highly seasonal, and demand planning is how we stay ahead of it. We turn sales data and commercial insight into the forecasts that drive production and inventory decisions across Europe.

As Demand Planner, you will be a core Subject Matter Expert in our rapid S&OP development. Reporting to the Head of Demand Planning, you will bridge top-line commercial forecasts with item-level operational reality. You will validate B2C category forecasts, own item planning, establish B2B forecasting, and improve forecast phasing across our peak cycles. This is a high-impact role where you will build quality into our demand process and support operational readiness.

How you embrace curiosity daily

Validate and check Commercial & Marketing's monthly, weekly, and daily category top-line forecasts against run rates, plans, and customer strategies

Challenge forecast assumptions constructively across key markets and products when inputs diverge from historical trends or operational reality

Own the detailed item planning process, splitting category forecasts into granular sub-category and item variant forecasts across Sales, Volume and ASP, providing item sales mix and margin visibility, and Operations with accurate production requirements

Drive continuous improvement in weekly and daily forecast phasing, reviewing and validating sales forecasts against promotional mechanics, seasonal uplift spikes, and Last Order Dates for key gifting events

Build pragmatic models and tools that help forecast owners submit higher-quality phasing inputs

Take end-to-end ownership of forecasting for B2B vendors, integrating these streams into the central S&OP process

How you make your mark

In this role, you will deliver real impact across our supply chain and business objectives

Support robust commercial consensus by bringing planning expertise to cross-functional partners

Validate and check

promotional phasing directly to Last Order Dates to improve peak season operational readiness

Provide volume and margin visibility through accurate, granular item forecasts aligned to category forecasts from Commercial & Marketing

Close unforecasted blind spots by building baseline forecasts for B2B channels

Prepare variance analysis and scenario reporting packs for monthly demand review meetings

Partner with Supply Planning so item-level forecast changes translate smoothly into capacity planning

Identify opportunities to refine planning spreadsheets and models to remove manual friction and improve data integrity

What you bring to the team

Three to five years of dedicated Demand Planning experience in a fast-paced environment like FMCG, Retail, or E-Commerce

Proven track record of managing item-level planning, mix modeling, and promotional uplift analysis

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer - Data Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Woven by Toyota  is enabling Toyota’s once-in-a-century transformation into a mobility company. Inspired by a legacy of innovating for the benefit of others, our mission is to challenge the current state of mobility through human-centric innovation — expanding what “mobility” means and how it serves society.

Our work centers on four pillars: AD/ADAS, our autonomous driving and advanced driver assist technologies; Arene, our software development platform for software-defined vehicles; Woven City, a test course for mobility; and Cloud & AI, the digital infrastructure powering our collaborative foundation. Business-critical functions empower these teams to execute, and together, we’re working toward one bold goal: a world with zero accidents and enhanced well-being for all.

Team

Our data platform team is working on accelerating autonomous driving by providing access to petabytes of data collected by our fleet of autonomous and non-autonomous vehicles. Efficient, fast and cost-effective access to data at large scale is key to tackle the hardest problems in AD/ADAS, from developing the Machine Learning (ML) models for perception and prediction of human driving patterns, to increasing the sophistication of our validation and simulation by identifying rare and interesting real-world driving situations. The data ecosystem developed by the London team is a key building block for developing and testing modern AD/ADAS products that will impact millions of customers.

Our ML and Data pipelines are built on-top of the open-source Flyte orchestration framework and are deployed to AWS. Pipeline code is written in Python. We use SQS and Kafka to automate data connections and leverage BigQuery and ElasticSearch for data storage. We believe strongly in automation and testing to ensure delivery of robust and correct systems.  We are a distributed team, working in the UK and US.

Who are we looking for?

The London Data Infrastructure team is looking for engineers who are passionate about and enable the next generation of automotive software development. The right candidate will have excellent communication skills, solid coding skills, broad knowledge of software development across areas such as Data Infrastructure and Warehouses, Data Ingestion, Compute Frameworks, Observability and Build Infra.

Responsibilities:

Work on high-impact projects and innovate new solutions to problems in the self-driving space.

Work with Computer Vision and Machine Learning engineers on high-impact projects and innovate new solutions to problems in the self-driving space.

Understand the complex data requirements of modern ML development and tailor our data ecosystem to these needs.

Build efficient data pipelines for ingestion from the vehicle fleet.

Work on distributed systems that serve, process and transform large quantities of data in the cloud

Mentor junior engineers in their day to day work

Design the long term strategy for several of our products

Minimum Qualifications

Arene’s goal is to open vehicle programming to everyone by simplifying vehicle software development and increasing deployment frequency without compromising safety and security. Arene aims to significantly improve how vehicles are designed and developed, and we’re working closely with Toyota to realize this goal in its next-generation vehicles.

A major component of the Arene Engineering team’s mission is to streamline software delivery and enhance operational speed in the automotive industry by developing innovative test, emulation, and simulation systems. We aim to facilitate quicker software releases and elevate the overall quality of automotive solutions, maintaining an uncompromised commitment to safety. The Arene organization is growing, and we are establishing an engineering center in London, UK, to strengthen our global team.

We are looking for software engineers who are excited to help build a state-of-the-art automotive platform that is “software first”. We envision the Arene platform will change the way vehicles are made. The ideal candidate will have a passion for technology and thrive in a fast-paced environment. Our team is developing tools and systems using modern software techniques. We need software engineers who excel at building robust software systems to solve challenging problems at scale.

The ideal candidate would have a considerable background in developing complex software with modern C++ over embedded systems.

Implement, deliver and refine Arene SDK software components for users to interact seamlessly with the vehicle systems

Collaborate with global teams to accelerate and improve Arene software development

At least 2 years of experience with modern C++ (C++14/17 and above).

An autonomous driving system typically comprises Sensing, Perception, Localization, Planning, and Control components. Our scope of work also encompasses the quality management of sensor data for post-processing activities and the operational management of calibration for our autonomous driving test vehicles.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

The Sensor & Calibration sub-team is seeking a Software Engineer to support the development of ground truth sensor calibration & data validation tools that live in the cloud and fuel our next-generation autonomous driving systems.

The selected candidate will be responsible for accelerating our calibration & data validation systems as well as maintaining & improving its infrastructure used across multiple teams. jobs.title: Senior Treasury Manager - Safeguarding & Cash Management for UK
jobs.description:
Nium provides global infrastructure for real-time cross-border payments.

We were founded on the mission to deliver the global payments infrastructure of tomorrow, today. Our platform enables banks, fintechs, and global businesses to move money instantly, everywhere.

Co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore with offices in 14 markets worldwide, we are entering one of the most exciting chapters in our journey. In March 2026, we delivered the largest month in our 11-year history with record revenue, record volumes, and EBITDA profitability. Today, Nium moves nearly $60B in payments annually, almost entirely for enterprises, while continuing to strengthen an already healthy balance sheet.

It is an incredible time to join us, and we are only just getting started.

Our payout network spans 190+ countries and 100 currencies, with 100 + corridors in real time. We power seamless transfers to accounts, wallets, and cards, support local collections in 35 markets, and as

a principal card issuer on Visa, Mastercard, Discover, and UATP, Nium issues over 50 million card tokens every year.

Backed by regulatory licenses in 40+ markets, we make it simple for our partners to onboard, integrate, and scale globally. This scale and innovation have earned us recognition as one of CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025, winner of Best Cross-Border Payments Solution at the PayTech Awards, and inclusion in FXC Intelligence’s Top 100 Cross-Border Payments Companies list.

In 2024, we raised US$50 million in Series E funding at a US$1.4 billion valuation to accelerate network expansion, product innovation, and talent growth. With the B2B payments market projected to hit US$175 trillion by 2030, Nium offers ambitious builders the chance to shape the future of global money movement with the scale of a leader and the energy of a high-growth company.

We are hiring a Senior Manager to take ownership of safeguarding for NIUM's UK regulated entities, covering both emoney and payment services activities under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011, Payment Services Regulations 2017, and the FCA's CASS15 sourcebook. This is a senior, hands-on, first-line role combining regulatory ownership, treasury decision-making, and 4-eyes oversight of operational work across the group.

You will be the day-to-day authority on UK safeguarding compliance; running reconciliation checks, chairing the UK Safeguarding Committee, owning FCA reporting, and acting as the escalation point for safeguarding incidents. You will also make live decisions on UK cash management, diversification, and interest optimisation, working closely with Compliance and the Director of Safeguarding to keep UK processes aligned to group standards while staying compliant with UK-specific regulatory requirements.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Patient Advocacy & Communications Lead, EMEA
jobs.description:
Scholar Rock is delivering muscle-targeted breakthroughs to transform the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and other rare neuromuscular diseases where muscle atrophy remains a critical unmet need.

As a global leader in myostatin biology, a field focused on proteins that regulate muscle mass, the biopharmaceutical company is named for the visual resemblance of a scholar rock to protein structures. Our commitment to unlock fundamentally different treatment approaches is powered by broad application of a proprietary platform, which has developed novel monoclonal antibodies to modulate protein growth factors with extraordinary selectivity. Scholar Rock works every day to create new possibilities for patients through its highly innovative anti-myostatin program, including opportunities in additional rare neuromuscular diseases. Learn more about our neuromuscular franchise at

ScholarRock.com

3+ months rolling contract

Newbury, UK

About the role

We are seeking a CyberArk Architect to lead solution design for a large-scale, TSA-regulated Privileged Access Management (PAM) migration and merger consolidation programme. This is a hands-on architecture role spanning vault migration design, identity federation, and application onboarding strategy for an estate spanning thousands of accounts and 250+ dependent applications, delivered against a fixed regulatory deadline.

Key responsibilities

Migration & vault architecture

Design the end-to-end migration architecture from CyberArk v12.2 to v14.2, covering entity extraction (REST API primary, PACLI fallback), transformation, reconciliation, and staged loading into the target vault.

Define the staged-ingestion model: disabled import → CPM soft-verification → dual-run mirroring → forced rotation at cutover — ensuring no credential is exposed to a script or human during migration.

Own name-collision resolution, platform normalisation, and policy reconciliation rules between source and target environments.

Produce migration runbooks, RAID logs, and effort-sizing models across Safes, Accounts, Platforms, and Policies.

Application & credential provider (CP/CCP) strategy

Lead discovery to segment the 250+ dependent applications by integration pattern (CP agent, CCP centralised, Conjur, direct SSO) — the primary driver of onboarding sequencing and timeline risk.

Design the CP/CCP re-onboarding approach, including AppID re-provisioning, certificate/mTLS re-issuance, and phased cutover waves.

Define rollback and dual-run strategy per wave, including the read-only fallback window on the source vault.

Identity federation & MFA

Design PVWA federation to Entra ID via SAML/OIDC, including claims mapping from Entra groups to CyberArk Vault Users and Safe membership.

Architect the RSA SecurID → Entra MFA migration as a re-enrolment exercise, covering Conditional Access policy design and non-web/legacy client bridging (PrivateArk, PACLI, RADIUS-dependent flows).

Ensure High Side / Low Side segregation is preserved across all federation and migration data flows, with no entitlement detail crossing the DMZ boundary.

Governance, compliance & stakeholder leadership

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer, New Grad - UK Government
jobs.description:
A World-Changing Company

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

Forward Deployed Engineering is a radical commitment to the outcome. This is Palantir’s operating ethos. We pioneered this unique position, embedding engineers directly with our customers to tackle their most pressing challenges head-on. As an FDE, you’ll be at the intersection of world-changing problems and impactful technology, shaping solutions where they matter most.

From hospital beds to factory floors, Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) embed themselves in the customer’s reality until the problem is theirs. This requires walking many miles in a customer’s shoes, building past the perimeter of what the product currently offers, and deviating from every pre-existing formula to solve the problem. Whether that problem is “How do we predict and mitigate wildfire risks across a power grid?” or “How can we analyze and adapt a global supply chain to deliver critical parts on time?” You’ll use your technical expertise, creativity, and problem-solving skills to drive real-world impact.

Core Responsibilities

To solve mission-critical problems by deploying software and AI into the high stakes operations of the world’s leading institutions. This requires a ruthless commitment to truth-seeking and prioritizing real outcomes.

The work is difficult. The stakes are real. You will work in small, high-trust teams and own projects end-to-end, from the first conversation with a customer, to shipping the product that changes how they operate. You will embed with the customer, the chaos, and the consequences, and will be entrusted with real ownership to:

Collaborate with engineers to make architecture and design decisions

Wrestle with data at a scale that breaks assumptions and demands invention

Build custom applications, LLM workflows, and production solutions engineered for a specific customer's reality

Own relationships with stakeholders from the users in the weeds to the executives making the calls

As a New Grad, you will be entrusted with responsibility on day 1. You will not be handed a ticket queue. You will not be shielded from the customer, the chaos, or the consequences. FDEs are entrusted with real ownership, operating with real autonomy, and held to a real standard, no matter their tenure.

What We Value

The drive to solve your customer’s problem. This can translate to:

Going where you’re needed most  — Embed where and when it matters. Expect 25–50% travel, depending on team and location.

Agency  — You learn continuously, make decisions with incomplete information, and don't wait to be told what to do next.

jobs.description:
About The Role

We're looking for a software engineer, reliability-minded but still a builder, to own what happens in production to the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet. The platform team builds the manifest-driven API and controllers that let the inference team declare what they need, a cluster, a model deployment, a capacity change, and get it reconciled underneath. Your job is to keep that promise true in the real world: triaging InfiniBand issues when prefill and decode nodes stall exchanging KV cache over RDMA, diagnosing hero-model and LoRA-serving faults that don't show up in generic health checks, and extending the automated self-healing system so each new failure mode becomes a permanent fix instead of a recurring page.

The core value we're after is keeping the decoupling real even when things break, and keeping the fleet efficient without that efficiency becoming a new source of instability. You'll own SLOs and error budgets for inference serving, lead incident response, and turn what postmortems teach you into actual changes in the controllers and automation, not just updated runbooks. You'll also work the reliability side of capacity efficiency, since a mistuned defragmentation or bin-packing pass is itself a production risk. Strong candidates have hands-on production-reliability experience on large-scale distributed or GPU-serving systems, are comfortable troubleshooting InfiniBand/RDMA and Kubernetes controller/CRD-based platforms, and think about GPU infrastructure, and the tools that keep it reliable, as software to be engineered.

A product mindset applies: the on-call experience, the clarity of an alert, and the judgment built into an automated remediation are things you ship and iterate on.

Responsibilities

  • Operate the provisioning state machine in production: own the health of the host lifecycle pipeline, discovery, inference bring-up, GPU driver/CUDA validation, health checks, decommission/RMA, triaging stuck or failed state transitions at fleet scale and feeding real failure patterns back into how the states and transitions are designed.
  • Triage and extend automated self-healing: when the node-scanning and remediation platform misses something, a new failure mode, an InfiniBand issue in disaggregated prefill/decode serving, a GPU Xid variant, a hero-model or LoRA-specific fault, diagnose it live, drive the fix to production, and turn it into a new detection/remediation plugin so it's automatic the next time.
  • Own end-to-end reliability of the pipeline: hold the SLOs and error budgets for provisioning and fleet health, lead incident response when idempotency, retry, rollback, or drift assumptions break down in practice, and drive the systemic fix, not just the hotfix.
  • Partner with the inference/ML platform team from the production side: be the one who knows how real cluster

We're currently seeking passionate individuals who are excited about the opportunity to contribute to an industry-shaping company while growing their own skills and careers.

The opportunity

We're looking for a Director or VP of Product Marketing to lead that effort globally. This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can connect deep technical understanding with positioning, distribution and commercial results. The title will reflect the experience and scope of the person we hire.

A good product story matters, but a story alone isn't enough. jobs.title: Senior Producer, Art
jobs.description:
WHAT MAKES US EPIC?

At the core of Epic’s success are talented, passionate people. Epic prides itself on creating a collaborative, welcoming, and creative environment. Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating.

Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development.

PRODUCTION

What We Do

Whether it’s driving a vision from start to finish or collaborating with teams to inspire and deliver projects of Epic quality, Epic’s production teams take pride in consistently delivering world-class products and experiences.

What You'll Do

Help us take Fortnite Battle Royale to the next level. As a Senior Art Producer on the Fortnite production team, you'll partner with Art Directors, artists, and designers to drive fun, high-quality live content from concept through delivery. We need someone who's deeply organized, communicates clearly across disciplines, and thrives managing the schedules of multiple complex art projects. You should be passionate about games and technology, with a proven track record producing within artistic teams.

In this role, you will

  • Own the Schedule - Partner with art discipline leads, to help scope and schedule the desired work for the team. Build and maintain dependency-driven asset schedules to ensure the successful, on-time, release of content, to the Epic Art Quality bar
  • Center of Communication - Facilitate constant communication with the art production team, as well as cross-department production teams, providing transparency on asset status, risks, and opportunities. Ensure stakeholders have proper visibility into development and are informed of any changes that may impact their teams
  • Proactively Seek Resolution - Strong ability to identify problems, and propose solutions, for your team before they become roadblocks. Keeping a finger on the pulse of dependency deliverables, tech initiatives, and the project's high-level needs. Own the outcome of your area, and never wait to see if someone else will clear your path. Self-starter, you approach challenges creatively and methodically, seeing them through to the final resolution
  • Flexible Multitasker - Ability to handle multiple large production needs within your department or across small strike teams. Understanding how to identify and break down prioritizations, and keeping up strong communication via multiple outlets; IE email, slack, meetings, and development roadmaps
  • Facilitate Development Operations - Schedule team meetings, running dailies art reviews, as well as in-game content reviews, while providing actionable notes and follow up
